newsitem.title: IRELAND: Irish Mar credit growth 18.6pct yr/yr-Central Bank.
newsitem.headline: Irish Mar credit growth 18.6pct yr/yr-Central Bank.

text.p: The adjusted annual rate of growth of Irish private sector credit rose to 18.6 percent in March from 15.8 percent in February, central bank monthly statistics showed on Thursday.
The increase was predominantly Irish-pound denominated and not mortgage-related, the bank said.
It was boosted by some exceptional items and also a number of transactions, the timing of which was influenced by the end of the financial year.
As a result, the annual rate of increase in non-mortgage Irish-pound credit rose to 20.7 percent in March from 17.4 percent the previous month.
The annual rate of increase in residential mortgage lending was 14.3 percent in March against 14.0 percent in February.
"Adjusting for the effect of the securitisation of mortgages in December, this series has been relatively steady for some months now," the bank said.
It said private sector credit increased by 1,870 million or 5.3 percent in March and 1.2 billion of this was Irish-pound denominated.
Factors contributing to the increase in Irish pound credit included lending to the Agricultural Intervention Agency and some exceptional items, the bank said.

Residential mortgage lending accounted for 181 million of the increase in Irish-pound credit, of which around a fifth represented end-quarter postings of interest and other mortgages added a further 39 million.
The main contribution came from a number of large corporate transactions, some of which appeared to be tax-related, the bank said.
Broad money supply growth (M3E) rose by 320 million or 0.9 percent but the adjusted rate of growth of M3E fell to 16.2 percent in March from 16.6 percent in February.
